speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up. To understand your occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain specifically triggered by chewing suggests referred pain from the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), which is innervated by the same nerve as the ear. Could you tell me if you have noticed clicking, popping, or tenderness when you press on your jaw joint in front of your ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming; the combination of shooting ear pain on chewing and discomfort with earrings points toward a TMJ issue or nerve irritation affecting the ear canal. Given your recent tympanoplasty, could you tell me if you notice any redness, drainage, or swelling inside your ear, or if the pain is also present in your jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain on chewing and with earrings strongly suggests involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or TMJ dysfunction, but we must rule out a graft infection or granulation tissue before confirming. Do you feel any warmth, redness, or discharge from the right ear, and does pressing on your jaw joint reproduce the pain?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy and TMJ palpation.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Ear_Otoscopy.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Otoscopy shows a clean, intact right ear canal with no signs of warmth, redness, or discharge; tympanic membrane appears healthy. TMJ palpation reveals no tenderness in the mandibular area and no jaw clicking; however, right postauricular tapping causes tenderness in the right tonsillar area, suggesting involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve rather than active TMJ dysfunction or graft infection.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Nerve Entrapment/Neuralgia post-Tympanoplasty. The negative TMJ palpation and clean otoscopy rule out joint dysfunction and graft infection, while tenderness upon postauricular tapping localizes the pain to the nerve supplying the ear and tonsillar region.
